artboards.title: Option A — One chrome band  ·  CHOSEN

annotations.text:
TODAY, at 1366×1024 (12.9" iPad).

Three bands of chrome before any content — header 56, repo bar 27, pane title 45 — then three columns where two are fixed furniture: rail 268, pads 344. The transcript gets 754px of 1366.

What breaks: at 1194 (11" iPad landscape) width is below the 1200 `wide` breakpoint, so the rail is already a modal drawer. The layout the README describes only exists on the largest iPad.

Four separate navigation systems: header views, rail tabs (agents/mcps), pane sub-tabs, right-panel picker. "hooks" appears in two of them meaning different things — git hooks and Claude Code hooks.

OPTION A — One chrome band.  ← CHOSEN, and now built.
Axis: reclaim space, keep the three-column model.

Header and repo bar merge into one 56px row: status dot, identity, the checkout as a chip, the view tabs, the path, ⋮. The rail becomes ONE tree — repo ▸ worktree ▸ the agents living in it — so "which worktree is this agent in" is answered by position instead of a longest-prefix match read by eye, and the two 30vh scroll boxes collapse to one list. The pads column becomes a 56px strip of keys that expands on tap.

Transcript: 754 → ~1040px. 27px of vertical chrome recovered.

Tradeoff, stated honestly: still three columns, so it still falls apart below 1200. This is the smallest honest diff, not the boldest layout.

NOTE: this drawing is the icon-forward pass. The shipped code keeps the original TEXT tabs (FOCUS · GUARDRAILS · GIT · USAGE) and uses icons only in the right-hand strip — which is what was picked.

OPTION B — Agent-first, one surface.  NOT BUILT — rejected.
Axis: fewest persistent surfaces; the transcript IS the app.

The rail becomes a 76px seat strip; projects and MCPs go behind its folder key; the view lenses move into the pane's own title row; the prompt library becomes a sheet over the composer opened by "/".

Transcript: 754 → 1290px, one band of chrome, same layout down to a phone.

Why it lost: it makes the pads two gestures instead of one and hides the projects tree, and the seat strip is a bigger bet than the problem needed.

OPTION C — Multi-agent cockpit.  NOT BUILT.
Axis: the app is for watching SEVERAL agents, not one.

One or two agent panes side by side, each with its own view tabs — a transcript beside another repo's CI. Drag a seat chip in to add a pane. One command bar spans the width and targets the focused pane.

Still the only option that answers "is the other agent blocked?" without leaving the one you're reading — worth revisiting once A has settled, since A's rail already knows which agent is in which worktree.

Tradeoff: most work by far, and each transcript drops to ~630px.

ICON SET — in use, but only where A actually needs it: the collapsed right-hand strip (prompts / skills / hooks) and the rail's row types.

One stroke weight, 24px grid, currentColor so a seat's status hue drives its own glyph. No emoji, no fills.

The rule that keeps it from becoming a puzzle: an icon that is a NAVIGATION choice keeps its word. That is why A's view tabs stayed text — a row of four glyphs all meaning "a view of this checkout" is exactly the kind of thing nobody learns.
